messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: rstan as a package dependency
parts:
I'm creating an R package for internal use that depends on rstan, and I'm struggling with how to handle that dependency. It's considered a bad idea to call library() from within package code -- instead you include it in the Imports line in the DESCRIPTION file. But stan() and sampling() seem to require a prior explicit call to library(rstan) in order to work. If you just call rstan::stan() without previously issuing the command "library(rstan)", you get the following error:

    Error in .Object$initialize(...) : 
      could not find function "cpp_object_initializer"
    failed to create the sampler; sampling not done

I have tried creating a .onLoad() function in my package, with a call to loadNamespace("rstan"), but I still get the same error.

Another issue with creating a package is that you want to precompile the model files. I've never been able to figure out where the DLL actually gets stored or how to transfer it to another machine with the same architecture and OS.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan as a package dependency
parts:
I'm sure the RStan devs will help out here, but until then,
you can check out the RStanARM package, which keeps precompiled
models around and has RStan as a dependency:

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstanarm

I believe a public release is imminent, but not yet scheduled.

For those who haven't heard about RStanARM, it's a tool Jonah Sol Gabry
and Ben Goodrich are building for using the lme4 linear "mixed effects"
model description language for specifying a model and Stan
for inference (NUTS MCMC for Bayes, L-BFGS optimization for MLE, and
ADVI for variational inference).

- Bob
